title: Charge VAT on food
headline: Zero-rated food is the biggest relief in the tax system: £27.4bn.
description: Charge the standard 20% rate of VAT on food (most food is zero-rated; catering, alcohol, confectionery, crisps, hot food and soft drinks already pay 20%). HMRC puts the cost of the current relief at £27.4bn in 2025-26; that is the static cost of the relief, not a forecast of what charging VAT would raise.

baselinePolicy.text: Most food and drink for human consumption is zero-rated; catering, alcoholic drinks, confectionery, crisps and savoury snacks, hot food, sports drinks, hot takeaways, ice cream and soft drinks are standard-rated.

rawSource.note: HMRC's estimate of the cost of the relief in 2025-26 (its latest year), carried forward with the OBR's VAT receipts path.

uprating.head: vat
uprating.note: The 2025-26 relief cost is applied from the start year and scaled by the OBR's VAT receipts forecast (ADR-0004).

caveats: HMRC: "These figures should be interpreted as estimates of the amount of relief which is claimed and subsequently granted each year. These estimates do not represent the gain to the exchequer should a relief be abolished." The toggle shows that static cost as revenue; the true yield would be lower once buyers respond and would depend on transitional arrangements.
HMRC's description of the relief: Zero rating of most food (including cold food for takeaway).

considerations.text: The figure is the cost of the relief with today's spending patterns. Charging VAT would raise prices, so people would buy less of these goods and more of others; HMRC's ready reckoner for the standard rate builds in such responses, but its relief cost estimates do not.

Zero and reduced rates are among the largest reliefs in the tax system: HMRC costs food at £27.4bn, new dwellings £14.6bn, domestic fuel and power £7.0bn, domestic passenger transport £5.8bn, children's clothing £2.3bn and printed matter £1.7bn in 2025-26. Who bears a change depends on how much of their spending households put on these goods, which this tool does not model.

interactions.text: The relief cost is valued at today's 20% standard rate; changing the standard rate changes what these toggles would raise.
